messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] about logistic regression
messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] about logistic regression
messages.body_plain:
Logistic regression is also applicable in situations where you're trying to model a rate or parameter which range from 0 to 1.What's actually going on is a generalized linear model <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_linear_model>, in particular the binomial with a logit link.

What we're observing is counts of cytosines (methylated) and thymine (methylated) at each site, which can be modeled as coming from a binomial distribution, where n is equal to the number of reads at that site. The logit function is the link function, which takes the underlying rate parameter (of the binomial), and models it's transform as a linear function of the independent data, in this case the sample treatments. We then test for whether the parameter for the treatment is significantly different from 0, and do FDR at the end.
